title: Rasgrp1 mutation increases naïve T-cell CD44 expression and drives mTOR-dependent accumulation of Helios+ T cells and autoantibodies
abstract: 10.7554/eLife.01020.001 Missense variants are a major source of human genetic variation. Here we analyze a new mouse missense variant, Rasgrp1 , with an ENU-mutated EF hand in the Rasgrp1 Ras guanine nucleotide exchange factor. Anaef Rasgrp1 mice exhibit anti-nuclear autoantibodies and gradually accumulate a CD44 Anaef hi Helios + PD-1 + CD4 + T cell population that is dependent on B cells. Despite reduced Rasgrp1-Ras-ERK activation in vitro, thymocyte selection in Rasgrp1 is mostly normal in vivo, although CD44 is overexpressed on naïve thymocytes and T cells in a T-cell-autonomous manner. We identify CD44 expression as a sensitive reporter of tonic mTOR-S6 kinase signaling through a novel mouse strain, Anaef chino , with a reduction-of-function mutation in Mtor . Elevated tonic mTOR-S6 signaling occurs in Rasgrp1 naïve CD4 Anaef + T cells. CD44 expression, CD4 + T cell subset ratios and serum autoantibodies all returned to normal in Rasgrp1 Anaef Mtor double-mutant mice, demonstrating that increased mTOR activity is essential for the chino Rasgrp1 T cell dysregulation.
